title: Letters A to Z
length_note: The alphabet has 26 letters. Each class covers about three letters, which is small enough to hold in mind and short enough to finish without getting tired. That gives eight classes of three letters (A to X), then a ninth class for the last two letters (Y and Z). A tenth class reviews the whole alphabet. Letters stay in alphabet order so the course matches the order learners will meet elsewhere. Each letter gets its upper and lower case shape, its sound, and a familiar picture word. Adults also get a grown-up word to connect with daily life. Classes run 8 to 12 minutes, with the review at 12 minutes. Each letter gets about 3 minutes, and the first class has a little extra time to explain how the lessons work.

classes.title: A, B, C: Your First Letters
classes.goal: Say the name, sound and a familiar word for A, B and C, and point to both the upper case and lower case of each.
topics: How each class works: see the letter, say its name, hear its sound, match a word
A, a: name, sound, apple (grown-up word: address)
B, b: name, sound, familiar word
C, c: name, sound, familiar word, with the common sound first
Upper case and lower case side by side

classes.title: Review: Find and Say Any Letter
classes.goal: Pick out any letter in upper or lower case, say its name and sound, and give a familiar word for it.
topics: Mixed upper and lower case practice across all 26 letters
Name, sound and word for letters chosen at random
Look-alike letters: b/d, p/q, I/l
Finding letters in real words, such as a name or an address
Marking which letters feel easy and which need another go
